sources.entry: MantisBT - Bug tracker, fits best for software development. (Demo, Source Code) GPL-2.0 PHP

summary.one_liner: MantisBT is a PHP-based web bug tracker that runs on a web server with MySQL or PostgreSQL, listed under ticketing in awesome-selfhosted.
summary.what_it_does: The README is short and mostly covers install, upgrade, and configuration rather than features. It describes a web-served PHP application backed by MySQL 5.5.35+, PostgreSQL 9.2+, or another supported database. Installation is done through a browser: a compatibility check page, then a database install/upgrade page where you choose the database type, enter credentials, and run the install. Upgrades are done by extracting a fresh tarball, copying configuration files over, and running the upgrade page. Configuration lives in config_inc.php, with defaults in config_defaults_inc.php, and the README points to an administration guide in the doc/ directory for full documentation. The README itself does not list specific bug-tracking features.
use_cases: host a ticketing system on a web server
how_to_run: Extract the tarball into a location readable by your web server
Open your browser and navigate to the MantisBT admin check page to verify web server compatibility
Navigate to the installer in your browser to start the database installation
Select the database type and enter database credentials, then click install/upgrade
Copy the default configuration to config/config_inc.php if the web server lacks write access
Remove the admin directory from the installation path before going live
notable: Browser-based installer and upgrader that handles database schema setup
Configuration overrides via config/config_inc.php without touching default files
Supports custom strings, relationships, functions, and constants through custom_*_inc.php override files
Full administration guide shipped in the doc/ directory in text, PDF, and HTML
caveats: Requires a PHP web server and a supported database; not a standalone app
The README has no screenshots or feature list; the admin guide in doc/ holds the detail
Upgrades require a clean extraction rather than overwriting an existing install
